If it does, serve TH-44/FranQwen3.8-27B-NVFP4-DFlash2 with --speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","model":"z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2","num_speculative_tokens":7}' at util 0.31, with flashinfer autotune still disabled, and check free memory >= 15 GiB. Keep the original Pro container so you can roll back.

kept.title: Build a 15-minute Uzbek A/B eval before changing prompts or models (UzLiB subset plus your own agent tasks)
kept.what_to_change: Clone github.com/tahrirchi/uzlib. Its README documents vLLM support through an OpenAI-compatible endpoint (run_uzlib.py --model_name ..., with the model config in utils.py). Point it at :8000 (Gemma) and :8001 (Qwen3.8). For speed, use a random 150-question subset. Add a second small set of 30 of your own prompts: 10 trick or logic questions, 10 'needs a fresh number' questions where the correct behaviour is to call search or the CBU tool, 5 OCR/table cases and 5 long-form answers. Score them automatically: tool called yes/no, number matches the tool output, share of Cyrillic characters in the answer (regex [Ѐ-ӿ]), repeated n-grams (loop detector), thinking-token count and wall time. Every later recommendation is A/B'd with this script.
kept.expected_gain: No direct gain. It turns the other changes from guesswork into measurable deltas. With 4B active parameters and decode around 50 tok/s, 150 multiple-choice questions take about 3-6 minutes.
evidence: https://github.com/tahrirchi/uzlib (README: vLLM-served models supported, temperature 1.0 / top_p 0.95 template)
https://github.com/tahrirchi/uzlib/blob/main/LEADERBOARD.md (Gemma 4 26B A4B 0.548, Gemma 4 31B 0.554, Qwen3.8 27B 0.396, Qwen3.5 35B A3B 0.380, NeuronAI 4B 0.662)
https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.11020 (TUMLU, ACL 2025: Uzbek is among the weakest Turkic languages for LLMs)
kept.applies_to_our_stack: Works unchanged against the vLLM 0.31 OpenAI endpoints. UzLiB measures linguistic and grammar knowledge, not agent ability, so the 30 custom agent prompts matter more for Sarob. Run it while no one is chatting, because there is only one GPU.
kept.risk: Low. The only cost is about 1-2 hours of setup once. A UzLiB score alone can mislead: a high linguistics-quiz score does not mean fluent tool-using answers.
kept.test_plan: Run the baseline on Gemma :8000 with the current Sarob system prompt. Save a JSON with accuracy, tool-call rate, Cyrillic %, loop rate, median thinking tokens and p50/p90 latency. Re-run after each change below. A change is accepted only if quality is not lower and latency is not higher.
kept.verifier_reason: Sound and low-risk, and it is a prerequisite for every other change. It uses only the standard OpenAI-compatible endpoints, so nothing version-specific needs to exist in vLLM 0.31. The regex [Ѐ-ӿ] covers U+0400-U+04FF, which is fine for Cyrillic. Caveats: (1) UzLiB's default sampling of temp 1.0 / top_p 0.95 adds noise to a 150-question subset. For A/B, use a fixed seed or temperature 0, or run 2-3 repeats, otherwise deltas under about 4 points are noise. (2) The 30 agent prompts must go through Open WebUI, or the same tool loop with the same system prompt and thinking_token_budget. Raw endpoint calls skip tools, memory and the system prompt, so they do not measure Sarob. (3) Read thinking-token counts from the reasoning_content length or the usage delta, because the gemma4 parser splits them out. (4) The leaderboard numbers quoted are the researcher's citations and were not independently verified here.
kept.corrected_change: Same plan, but: run UzLiB with temperature=0 (or a fixed seed plus 3 repeats) for A/B. Run the 30 agent prompts through the Open WebUI API (/api/chat/completions with the Sarob model id), or through the Telegram bot's loop, so tools, system prompt and budgets are included. Log reasoning tokens from the reasoning_content field. Treat a delta under about 4 UzLiB points as noise.

kept.title: Keep Gemma (not Qwen3.8) as the Uzbek voice; let Qwen3.8 Pro think in English and verify its Uzbek output
kept.what_to_change: In the Open WebUI 'Sarob Pro' model system prompt, add one line in English: 'Reason internally in English. Write the final answer only in Uzbek (Latin script), natural literary style; keep numbers, names and code unchanged.' Do not switch Pro to Gemma-4-31B dense: it scores only +0.005 on UzLiB and would be slower than Qwen3.8 on GB10's ~273 GB/s bandwidth. If the eval shows Qwen3.8 Uzbek errors that users notice, the fallback is to route hard reasoning questions to Pro and simple conversational or language questions to Gemma Sarob. Open WebUI model presets can do this; no code is needed.
kept.expected_gain: UzLiB (Oct 2026 leaderboard): Gemma 4 26B A4B 0.548 vs Qwen3.8 27B 0.396, a 15-point gap in Uzbek linguistic competence. Gemma is therefore the better default Uzbek writer, and Pro's value is reasoning, not language. Thinking in English should also shorten Pro's reasoning traces (estimated 20-40% fewer thinking tokens; unverified), which at 21-31 tok/s could save several seconds per Pro answer.
evidence: https://github.com/tahrirchi/uzlib/blob/main/LEADERBOARD.md
https://arxiv.org/html/2502.11020v2 (TUMLU: CoT generally helps strong models in Uzbek: Claude 3.5 +3.7, Gemini 1.5 Pro +1.9; it hurt Llama 3.1 70B -17.4)
kept.applies_to_our_stack: This is a pure prompt change in Open WebUI 0.12 model settings, and the reasoning stays in the qwen3 reasoning parser's think block. The thinking_token_budget of 1024 stays and is more useful when the reasoning is in compact English. Caveat: I found no published number for Qwen3.8's English-vs-Uzbek thinking efficiency, so the token saving is an estimate to verify.
kept.risk: Low to medium. The answer may occasionally leak English words or calques. Watch the 'English-word ratio' in the eval.
kept.test_plan: Run the 30 custom prompts and 100 UzLiB questions on Pro with and without the line. Compare accuracy, mean reasoning tokens (usage.completion_tokens minus visible answer tokens) and time to final answer. Have one native speaker blind-rate 10 answers for fluency.
kept.verifier_reason: A pure prompt change: cheap, reversible and testable. Three corrections: (1) Qwen3-family models already reason mostly in English even for non-English prompts, so the claimed 20-40% thinking-token saving is speculative and may be about 0. The real value is the explicit 'final answer in Uzbek Latin' rule. (2) The claim that 'Open WebUI model presets can do this routing, no code needed' is wrong. Open WebUI 0.12 has no automatic per-question routing between models. The user picks Sarob or Pro manually. Automatic routing needs a Pipe/Manifold function or a pipeline with a classifier call, which adds latency. (3) Not switching Pro to a dense 31B is correct for GB10 bandwidth.
kept.corrected_change: Add to the Sarob Pro system prompt: 'Reason internally in English. Write the final answer only in Uzbek (Latin script)...'. Expect little or no thinking-token reduction, so measure it. For routing, keep manual model choice (Sarob for everyday questions, Pro for hard reasoning) rather than claiming presets auto-route. Automatic routing would need a custom Pipe function and should be A/B'd for the latency it adds.

kept.title: Restructure the Sarob system prompt: English rules and tool policy, Uzbek persona and style block, glossary, and two short exemplar dialogues (prefix-cached, so TTFT is unchanged)
kept.what_to_change: Split the current ~1.8k-token Uzbek prompt into three parts. (a) An English block of about 400-600 tokens with hard rules: 'ALWAYS call search/CBU/SQL tool before stating any price, rate, date, statistic or current fact; never invent numbers; if tool fails, say so'; 'For trick/logic questions, think step by step before answering'; 'Search queries: also query in Russian and English when Uzbek results are thin; translate findings into Uzbek'. (b) An Uzbek block: persona plus output rules: 'Faqat oʻzbek lotin alifbosida yoz; oʻ va gʻ harflarida ʻ (U+02BB) belgisidan, tutuq belgisida ʼ (U+02BC) dan foydalan; kirill harflarini ishlatma, foydalanuvchi kirillchada yozsa ham, agar u soʻramasa'. (c) A glossary of 30-60 domain terms you see the model get wrong (e.g. exchange rate = valyuta kursi, spreadsheet = jadval/Excel fayli) plus two short exemplar Q→tool→answer turns showing the desired tone and the 'search before numbers' behaviour. Keep the whole block static at the top so vLLM --enable-prefix-caching hits it. Do not put dates or memory content above it.
kept.expected_gain: Quality: fewer invented numbers and fewer slips into Cyrillic or inconsistent apostrophes. The expected gain on tool-call rate for factual questions is moderate (estimate +10-30% on the 'needs fresh number' set; to be measured). Latency: English instructions take roughly 30-50% fewer tokens than the same rules in Uzbek (Gemma's tokenizer fragments agglutinative Uzbek more), and the prefix is cached, so TTFT stays around 0.15-0.25 s.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2410.13153 (Better to Ask in English: English instructions beat low-resource-language instructions for GPT-4/Llama2/Gemini)
https://arxiv.org/html/2502.11020v2 (TUMLU cites prior work that English prompts did not help on knowledge MCQ, so evidence is mixed; A/B required)
NAACL 2025 Liu et al. (summarised via search): native-language prompting better for culture-related tasks, so keep persona and style in Uzbek
https://timesca.com/uzbekistan-alphabet-reform-latin-cyrillic/ (both scripts still widely used, so the model sees mixed training data)
kept.applies_to_our_stack: Applies to the Open WebUI 0.12 model system prompt and to the Telegram bot's agent loop, which should use the same text so both benefit. Native function calling is unaffected. Gemma 4 handles mixed-language system prompts well in general, but I found no Gemma-4-specific Uzbek study, so this rests on general multilingual evidence.
kept.risk: Medium. English rules can nudge answers toward translationese or English words. Mitigate with the explicit Uzbek output rules and exemplars. A longer prompt increases memory per sequence slightly, which is negligible at max-num-seqs 8.
kept.test_plan: A/B the old and new prompt on the 30 custom prompts (3 runs each, temp as deployed). Metrics: tool-call rate on fact questions, numbers matching tool output, Cyrillic %, apostrophe consistency, trick-question accuracy and first-token latency (should be unchanged after the first warm request). About 10 minutes.
kept.verifier_reason: Plausible and testable. It targets the observed problems (invented numbers, trick questions, Cyrillic drift), and English rules cost fewer tokens. Caveats on the prefix-cache claim: Open WebUI injects dynamic content into the system message. The memory feature adds the user's memories as context, RAG/file context and {{CURRENT_DATE}}-style variables expand per request, and with native function calling the Gemma 4 chat template renders tool schemas in the system turn. So 'static at the top' only holds if the operator checks the final rendered prompt and the dynamic parts land after the static block. TTFT is already 0.15-0.25 s, so the real gain is quality, not latency. Two exemplar dialogues add maybe 300-600 tokens, which is fine. Prefix caching also needs the tool set to stay stable across requests; toggling tools per chat breaks the cache.
kept.corrected_change: Same restructure. Additionally, verify the rendered prompt (log one request body at vLLM with --enable-log-requests, or in an Open WebUI inlet filter). Confirm that memory and date injections and any {{CURRENT_DATE}} variables come after the static rules, glossary and exemplars. Keep the enabled tool set constant so the tool-schema part of the prefix stays cache-stable. Use the identical text in the Telegram bot.

kept.title: Add an Open WebUI outlet filter for Uzbek script normalization and loop/Cyrillic detection (cheap, no GPU cost)
kept.what_to_change: Create an Open WebUI Function of type Filter (Admin > Functions) with an outlet(body) that edits the last assistant message. (1) Normalize oʻ and gʻ variants: replace o', o`, o‘, o’ and gʻ variants with U+02BB, and use U+02BC for the tutuq belgisi. Pick one convention; the plain ASCII apostrophe is also acceptable if you prefer search-friendliness. Skip code blocks and URLs. (2) If more than 3% of letters are Cyrillic and the user did not write in Cyrillic, transliterate Cyrillic to Latin with a deterministic rule-based transliterator. Uzbek Cyrillic→Latin is mostly deterministic; the reverse is not (see arXiv 2205.09578). (3) Detect repeated paragraphs (same 40+ char line 3+ times) and truncate the repeats. Enable the filter globally or on Sarob, Sarob Tez and Pro. Apply the same function in the Telegram bot's post-processing.
kept.expected_gain: Removes visible script-mixing and duplicate-text artifacts at zero model latency (microseconds of Python). It does not fix the reasoning behind a loop, but it removes the user-visible symptom.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2205.09578 (Uzbek alphabet transliteration tool; Cyrillic→Latin mapping rules)
https://arxiv.org/html/2502.11020v2 (Uzbek web data is evenly split Latin/Cyrillic, so models drift between scripts)
https://docs.openwebui.com (Functions: Filter inlet/outlet)
kept.applies_to_our_stack: Open WebUI 0.12 Filter functions run outlet after the stream completes. The live stream may briefly show the raw text, and the normalized version is what gets stored and shown on refresh. If real-time correction is needed, the 'stream' hook in filters (present in recent Open WebUI versions) can rewrite chunks; check that it exists in 0.12 before relying on it. Hard-banning Cyrillic with vLLM logit_bias is possible in principle (vLLM supports logit_bias, bad_words and allowed_token_ids), but it would need thousands of token IDs per request. Not recommended unless the eval shows frequent leakage.
kept.risk: Low. Russian-language quotes, names or user requests in Cyrillic could be wrongly transliterated, so skip when the user's own message is Cyrillic or contains 'kirill'.
kept.test_plan: Feed 20 saved real answers, including known Cyrillic or apostrophe-mixed ones, through the filter offline and diff. Then enable it and confirm the eval's Cyrillic % drops to about 0 and the loop rate on stored messages falls. 15 minutes.
kept.verifier_reason: Open WebUI Filter functions support inlet/outlet, and recent versions also have a stream(event) hook, so this is feasible in 0.12 at about zero latency. Risks to handle: (1) Normalizing to U+02BB/U+02BC changes the text that goes back to the model in later turns and that is copied into searches. SearXNG queries and most Uzbek web text use ASCII ' or ‘, so U+02BB can hurt search recall if the model copies it into tool queries. Restrict normalization to display, or choose the ASCII apostrophe. (2) Cyrillic transliteration must skip code blocks, URLs, quoted Russian text, and user requests in Cyrillic or Russian. (3) Truncating loops only hides the symptom. The root cause should also be addressed with sampling, e.g. a modest repetition_penalty of about 1.05 or presence_penalty in the model's advanced params, A/B'd with the eval.
kept.corrected_change: Implement as described, but default to the ASCII apostrophe (o', g') for search-friendliness, or apply U+02BB only to the final displayed text and not to tool-call arguments. Skip fenced code, inline code, URLs and lines that are mostly Russian. Only transliterate when Cyrillic is above 3% and the user's last message is Latin. In parallel, A/B repetition_penalty 1.05 for Gemma in the Open WebUI model's advanced params to reduce loops at the source.

kept.title: Do not adopt full translate→think→translate or an Uzbek fine-tune for the main path; at most, trial NeuronAI-4B offline as a grammar checker
kept.what_to_change: Do not add a pipeline that translates the user's question to English, answers, and translates back. It adds two extra generation passes (estimated +2-6 s for typical answers at 50 tok/s, about doubling simple-question latency) and loses cultural and idiomatic nuance. Native-language prompting wins on culture-related tasks (NAACL 2025), and TUMLU found English prompts gave no gain. The English-reasoning instruction in the earlier recommendations gets most of the benefit at no extra latency. On fine-tunes: no Gemma-4 Uzbek LoRA or fine-tune exists as of Oct 2026 in my search; the Uzbek fine-tunes are Llama, Mistral and Qwen bases. NeuronUz/NeuronAI-4B (Qwen3.5-4B base, Uzbek tokenizer retrofit plus continued pretraining plus SFT) reports UzLiB 0.662, above Gemma 4 26B (0.548), but it is a 4B dense model with unknown tool-calling or agent ability. If curious, run it on the UzLiB subset and as an optional 'Uzbek proofread' action button (Open WebUI Action function) that the user triggers manually. Never put it inline on every answer.
kept.expected_gain: Avoids a latency regression of 2-6 s per message. The optional proofreader could improve the grammar of long texts (letters, official documents) on demand. Its benefit is unmeasured; the 0.662 is the publisher's own claim.
evidence: https://huggingface.co/NeuronUz/NeuronAI-4B
https://huggingface.co/NeuronUz/NeuronAI-Uzbek/blob/main/README.md (UzLiB 0.662 vs 0.345 base Qwen3-4B; +22.5% tokenizer efficiency; self-reported)
https://github.com/tahrirchi/uzlib/blob/main/LEADERBOARD.md
https://arxiv.org/html/2502.11020v2
https://preview.aclanthology.org/landing_page/2025.loresmt-1.9.pdf (selective pre-translation of prompt parts)
kept.applies_to_our_stack: A third vLLM engine for a 4B BF16 model needs about 8-10 GiB weights plus KV at --gpu-memory-utilization around 0.08-0.10. This fits alongside 0.35+0.28 only if the >=15 GiB free margin still holds; check with free -g after start. Gemma-4 MoE NVFP4 with LoRA in vLLM is not something I could verify as supported, so training your own Uzbek LoRA is not a quick win.
kept.risk: Low if you skip it. A medium memory risk if you run the third engine; start it at low util and with --max-num-seqs 2.
kept.test_plan: Optional, and not on the critical path. Start NeuronAI-4B on :8002 with --gpu-memory-utilization 0.08 --max-model-len 8192, run 150 UzLiB questions, then have it proofread 10 Gemma long-form answers and blind-rate them against the originals. Stop the container afterwards if there is no clear win.
kept.verifier_reason: Rejecting the translate round-trip pipeline is correct for latency on a single user, and the advice is mostly 'don't do X', so it is low risk. The optional NeuronAI-4B trial has a memory problem. 0.35+0.28 = 0.63 of about 121 GiB is roughly 76 GiB. Adding 0.08 (about 9.7 GiB) for a 4B BF16 model, whose weights alone are about 8 GiB, leaves only about 1-1.5 GiB for KV cache and activations. Startup may fail, or the engine works with almost no KV. On top of that come Open WebUI, Ollama bge-m3, the CPU reranker, Playwright and Jupyter, so the >=15 GiB margin is tight. This should be a strictly temporary test: stop the Pro engine during it, or use util of about 0.10 with --max-model-len 8192 --max-num-seqs 2 --enforce-eager. The 0.662 UzLiB figure is self-reported. Strictly optional and lowest priority.
kept.corrected_change: Skip the translate pipeline (agreed). If you trial NeuronAI-4B, do it in a maintenance window. Stop the Qwen3.8 Pro container first, or check free -g for at least 25 GiB free. Launch with --gpu-memory-utilization 0.10 --max-model-len 8192 --max-num-seqs 2 --enforce-eager. Run the UzLiB subset and a 10-answer proofreading blind test, then stop it. Do not run it as a permanent third engine unless memory headroom of 15 GiB or more is verified with all services up.

kept.title: Add a thin proxy that chooses thinking on/off and the budget for every request, including each call inside a tool loop
kept.what_to_change:
Put a small streaming pass-through proxy (FastAPI or aiohttp, about 100 lines) on :8010 in front of Gemma :8000. Point both the Open WebUI connection and the Telegram bot at it. For each request it rewrites `chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking` and `thinking_token_budget`. Both are valid vLLM request fields: thinking_token_budget is a SamplingParam, and the gemma4 template defaults enable_thinking to false.
Rules, all regex/length heuristics, about 0 ms:
(a) Last message is role=='tool' (a post-tool turn inside the agent loop): enable_thinking=true, budget 128-256. Important: when thinking is on, the Gemma 4 template opens a thought channel after every tool response, so each tool round currently spends up to 512 thinking tokens (8-11 s at 46-61 tok/s).
(b) Last user message is short (under about 15 words), a greeting, chit-chat, a rewrite, a translation or a summary, with no digits or logic markers: enable_thinking=false.
(c) Images attached and the text asks to extract, OCR or make a table (jadval, Excel): enable_thinking=false or budget 128.
(d) Math, logic or trick markers (digits plus operators, nechta, qancha, hisobla, nega, isbotla, solishtir, agar ... bo'lsa, 'diqqat', riddle-like phrasing, multiple constraints): enable_thinking=true, budget 1024-1536.
(e) Everything else: budget 384.
Also always set max_tokens >= budget + 2048 so a forced cutoff never leaves an empty answer.
Do not do this with an Open WebUI Filter alone. inlet() runs once per user message, so it cannot give post-tool turns a different budget than the first call. A filter is fine for a first version that handles rules (b)-(e) only, by writing body['chat_template_kwargs'] and body['thinking_token_budget'].
Optional phase 2: if the heuristics misroute more than about 10% of a test set, add a 1-token classifier call to Gemma itself (enable_thinking=false, max_tokens=1, a 100-token prompt asking 'E/H'). Expected cost is about 60-120 ms on GB10. The DART-style double-draft router (arXiv 2606.23181) saves 32-73% of thinking tokens but needs 2 drafts, so it is too slow for a latency-first single user.
kept.expected_gain: Each thinking token costs about 17-22 ms at the measured decode speed. Simple questions: -512 thinking tokens, about 5-10 s saved (3-8 s goes to about 1.5-3 s). Web-search answers with 2-3 tool rounds: post-tool budget 512 -> 192 saves about 5-7 s per round, so roughly 10-20 s off the 20-60 s total. Trick and math questions get 2-3x more thinking than today, so they should be more accurate, at the cost of 10-20 s more on those questions only.
evidence: https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/features/reasoning_outputs/ (thinking_token_budget request param; chat_template_kwargs enable_thinking; Gemma 4 thinking off by default; reasoning_effort 'none' injects enable_thinking=false)
https://huggingface.co/google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it/raw/main/chat_template.jinja (enable_thinking default false; with thinking on, the generation prompt opens a thought channel after a tool response)
https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/api/vllm/v1/sample/thinking_budget_state/ (the budget resets after each end marker, so it applies per thinking section, i.e. per loop turn)
https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.28662 (AMIGO: in a multi-step agentic task, Gemma 4 31B with thinking was worse than without, 9.8% -> 7.5% verified correct, with more rounds)
https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.09282 (Qwen3.6 with thinking: mixed effect on tool use; calculator calls dropped from 4.21 to 1.19)
https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.23181 (DART adaptive budgets, -32-73% thinking tokens)
https://docs.openwebui.com/features/extensibility/plugin/functions/filter
kept.applies_to_our_stack: vLLM 0.31 honors per-request chat_template_kwargs and thinking_token_budget. The budget state machine is speculative-decoding aware, so it works with MTP. Open WebUI 0.12 forwards extra body fields to an OpenAI connection. One proxy also covers the Telegram bot. It is not version-locked to Open WebUI internals, and it adds no GPU memory. The Uzbek keyword list has to be built by the operator from real chat logs. Uncertainty: no published Gemma 4 benchmark measures post-tool thinking vs none. Only AMIGO hints that less thinking does not hurt agentic loops, so the post-tool budget must be A/B tested.
kept.risk: Low to medium. Misrouting a hard question to no-think brings back the trick-question failures, so keep (d) generous and default to 384, not 0. A proxy bug can break streaming, so pass the SSE bytes through untouched and modify only the request. Post-tool budget 0 might reintroduce tool skipping or looping, which is why the test plan includes it as a separate arm.
kept.test_plan: Build a 30-prompt Uzbek set: 10 easy (greetings, rewrite, translate), 10 that need tools (kurs, narx, yangilik), 10 trick or math. Run it through Open WebUI's API (/api/chat/completions) twice: via :8000 directly (current 512) and via the proxy. Log wall time, number of tool calls, and reasoning length (len(message.reasoning) per turn; vLLM logs completion tokens per request). Score correctness by hand. Then sweep the post-tool budget over {0, 128, 256, 512} on the 10 tool prompts only, about 3 min per arm. Accept when median latency drops at least 30% and correctness is not lower. Total time: about 15 min.
kept.verifier_reason: The fields exist. thinking_token_budget is a request-body sampling param in vLLM (confirmed in the reasoning_outputs docs), and chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking is honored per request. Using a proxy instead of only an inlet filter is the right call for per-iteration control and for the Telegram bot, and it adds no GPU memory. The main flaw is a prefix-cache trap. Gemma 4 turns thinking on by putting a <|think|> token at the start of the system turn, so flipping enable_thinking changes the first tokens of the prompt. Prefix caching then misses on the whole 6k-15k (up to 50k) prompt. Toggling between turns, or between calls inside one tool loop (rule a vs b/c), would force a full re-prefill each time, roughly 1-4 s or more on GB10. That eats much of the savings and contradicts the 0.15-0.25 s TTFT they measured. Default 384 and post-tool 128-256 are plausible but must be A/B tested. Also mind vLLM issue #39043: with enable_thinking=false, tool calls leak into the text.
kept.corrected_change: Keep enable_thinking=true fixed for every request (it already is) so the cached prefix with <|think|> stays the same. Route only through the per-request thinking_token_budget: easy/chit-chat/rewrite/translate/OCR-table 0-32, post-tool turns (last message role=='tool') 128-256, default 384, math/logic/trick 1024-1536. Set max_tokens >= budget + 2048. Only consider enable_thinking=false for a brand-new single-turn request with no tools (e.g. the Telegram short-reply path), and measure TTFT before and after to confirm the cache is not lost. Pass SSE through untouched. A first version can be an Open WebUI filter inlet that sets body['thinking_token_budget'] only.

kept.title: Send Gemma its own reasoning from earlier steps of the current tool loop (Open WebUI connection Provider = llama.cpp)

Per the Open WebUI docs, 'Default' omits structured reasoning when it rebuilds messages, inside tool-call loops as well. 'llama.cpp' sends it back as a top-level `reasoning_content` field on the assistant message. The Gemma 4 template reads message.reasoning or message.reasoning_content and renders it for assistant messages after the last user message (the current agent loop). Earlier turns are still dropped, as the model card recommends, so long chats do not grow. If you build the proxy from recommendation 1, it can do the same thing: copy the reasoning of the previous assistant turn in the same loop into `reasoning_content`.

Gemma currently loses its plan after every tool result, which plausibly causes re-planning, redundant searches and some of the looping you see. Expect fewer tool rounds on multi-step tasks; each round saved is worth 3-10 s. Extra prefill is a few hundred tokens per round, which costs milliseconds with prefix caching. Gain is unquantified; I found no published numbers specific to Gemma.

kept.title: Keep thinking-budget forcing exact: no transition phrase in reasoning_end_str, and guard max_tokens
kept.what_to_change: The vLLM docs suggest putting a wrap-up phrase into `--reasoning-config` reasoning_end_str (e.g. '...answer now.</think>'). Do not do this for Gemma. vLLM's ThinkingBudgetState detects a natural end only by matching the full end-token sequence. A multi-token phrase would therefore never be seen when Gemma closes with a bare `<channel|>`: counting would continue into the answer, and the phrase plus `<channel|>` would then be forced into the visible content. Keep reasoning_end_str exactly '<channel|>' as it is now. Put budget awareness in the system prompt instead, one Uzbek line such as 'Fikrlashni qisqa tut: faqat reja va tekshiruv, keyin javob ber.'. Make sure every request has max_tokens >= thinking_token_budget + 2048. Open WebUI's max_tokens per model, or the proxy, can enforce this; a low max_tokens is the documented cause of empty answers when the budget is consumed.
kept.expected_gain: Avoids a silent quality bug: answers with injected '<channel|>' or garbage text, or empty answers. Possibly a small cut in thinking length from the prompt line; unmeasured.
evidence: https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/api/vllm/v1/sample/thinking_budget_state/ (_find_last_sequence_index matches the whole think_end_token_ids sequence; forcing applies logit 1e9 to the next end token)
https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/features/reasoning_outputs/ (reasoning_end_str may include a transition phrase)
https://github.com/phishingupstream/vllm-thinking-budget (budget exhaustion leads to empty response and broken tool calls)
https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/25536 (Qwen3.6: reasoning consumes all max_tokens)
kept.applies_to_our_stack: Applies directly to the existing --reasoning-config on both engines in vLLM 0.31. This is my reading of the budget state source code; I have not seen a GitHub issue reproducing the phrase failure, so treat it as a strong caution rather than a confirmed bug.
kept.risk: None if nothing changes. The main action is not adopting a tempting doc example, plus a max_tokens check.
kept.test_plan: grep the current docker run for reasoning_end_str and confirm it is exactly '<channel|>' (Gemma) and '</think>' (Qwen). Send 5 hard prompts with thinking_token_budget=64 and max_tokens=1500. Each response must have a non-empty content and no '<channel|>' or '<|channel>' in content. About 5 min.
kept.verifier_reason: The vLLM docs do show a transition-phrase reasoning_end_str example (for Qwen3), so the caution is relevant. The concern follows from the budget state matching the whole end-token sequence: Gemma's natural end is a bare <channel|>, so a multi-token phrase would never be seen as a natural end. This is unconfirmed but cheap to respect, since the advice is mostly 'do not change'. The max_tokens >= budget + 2048 guard addresses a documented failure mode: empty answers when reasoning consumes max_tokens. The Uzbek 'keep thinking short' prompt line is harmless if appended to the end of the static system prompt once, since that keeps the prefix stable.
kept.corrected_change: Keep reasoning_end_str exactly '<channel|>' (Gemma) and '</think>' (Qwen). Enforce max_tokens >= thinking_token_budget + 2048 in the proxy or in Open WebUI model params. If the Uzbek brevity line is added, edit the system prompt once (one-time cache invalidation), not per request.

kept.title: For fact and number questions, inject a one-line 'tool first' hint into the user turn instead of thinking or tool_choice=required
kept.what_to_change: In the proxy, or an Open WebUI filter inlet, detect queries that need fresh or exact facts: kurs, narx, bugun, hozir, yangilik, statistika, years, currency names, 'qancha turadi'. For these, append a short suffix to the last user message, not to the system prompt, so the 1.8k system-prompt prefix stays cached. Example: '\n\n[Eslatma: aniq raqam/sana kerak — avval tegishli tool'ni chaqir, tool natijasisiz raqam yozma.]'. Keep thinking at the default 384 for these; they do not need 1024. Do NOT set tool_choice='required' in Open WebUI. Open WebUI reuses the same request params across its native tool loop, so 'required' would force a tool call on every iteration and the loop would never end. Also, in vLLM, 'required' uses structured-output JSON instead of the gemma4 tool parser, which is untested here. For trick questions, rely on routing to thinking with budget 1024+ (recommendation 1) rather than a 'self-check without thinking' prompt. I found no evidence that self-check prompts without thinking fix trick questions on Gemma 4.
kept.expected_gain: Directly targets 'skips tools and invents numbers'. The expected effect is a higher tool-call rate on fact queries; unquantified, so measure it. It adds about 0 ms; a suffix of about 30 tokens does not invalidate the prefix cache.
evidence: https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/features/reasoning_outputs/ (tool calls are parsed only from content; reasoning is separate)
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/39043 (Gemma 4 with enable_thinking=false: tool calls leak into chat text, so test the no-think tool path carefully)
https://docs.openwebui.com/features/chat-conversations/chat-features/reasoning-models (native tool loop rebuilds and resends messages each iteration)
kept.applies_to_our_stack: Works with Open WebUI 0.12 native function calling and the Telegram loop if done in the proxy. The keyword list is Uzbek-specific and must come from the operator's logs. Issue #39043 also matters for recommendation 1: if no-think routing (b) ever applies to tool-needed queries, watch for tool calls printed as text.
kept.risk: Low. Possible over-triggering of search on questions the model can answer, costing 3-6 s each. Mitigate by keeping the keyword list narrow.
kept.test_plan: Take 15 fact prompts where Gemma previously skipped tools. Run each with and without the suffix. Measure: was a tool called (count tool_calls in the response), are the numbers correct against CBU/SearXNG, and wall time. Pass if tool use rises to at least 90% and no-tool hallucinations drop. About 10 min.
kept.verifier_reason: The reasoning holds. Open WebUI's native loop resends the same params, so tool_choice='required' would force a tool call on every iteration. In vLLM, 'required' also goes through guided JSON rather than the gemma4 parser. Appending a roughly 30-token suffix to the last user message keeps the system-prompt prefix cached. The gain is unquantified, but the approach is cheap and directly targets the 'invents numbers' failure. The suffix must be applied the same way on every loop iteration, or the cache for the rest of the conversation is lost. Keep the Uzbek keyword list narrow so search does not over-trigger.
kept.corrected_change: Implement in the proxy (it also covers Telegram). Append the suffix to the last role=='user' message the same way on every request of the loop. Also make sure the suffix is not saved into chat history, so it does not pile up across turns.

kept.title: Check sampling defaults for each model; loops may be a sampling problem, not a thinking problem
kept.what_to_change: Google's Gemma 4 card recommends a single setting for all modes: temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, top_k 64. Check what Open WebUI actually sends (Workspace -> Models -> Sarob -> Advanced Params). Any repetition_penalty > 1.0 or a low temperature (<= 0.3) on a thinking model is a common cause of loops and repetition. Trade-off for latency: higher temperature lowers MTP acceptance. Also test temperature 0.7, and keep whichever gives the best loop rate × tok/s.

https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/features/reasoning_outputs/

kept.title: Cache-aware tiering: vary thinking_token_budget per message on Gemma (never toggle enable_thinking), and make Pro routing sticky per chat
kept.what_to_change: Inside route(): (a) If any message part has type image_url, or the message has attachments, always use Gemma (it has proven vision; Qwen3.8 vision is unverified). (b) Manual overrides: a message starting with '/tez' forces fast, '/pro' forces pro, '/o'yla' forces think. Strip the prefix before sending. (c) Fast tier for greetings, chit-chat, translation, rewriting and short factual questions (fewer than about 15 words, no digits or math, no 'nega', 'isbotla' or 'hisobla'). Set body['thinking_token_budget']=0 or 64. The think tier keeps 512. (d) Pro tier only when hard-reasoning or code keywords appear (isbotla, tahlil qil, algoritm, kod yoz, ```, solve, formulas) AND (the chat has fewer than about 4k tokens OR it is already on Pro). Store self.sticky[chat_id]='pro' and do not drop back to Gemma for the rest of that chat unless the user types /tez. (e) Never send chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking=false on the main request. Gemma 4 puts <|think|> in the system turn at position 0, so flipping it changes the very first tokens and invalidates the entire prefix cache for a 6-15k-token chat. Keep thinking enabled and set the budget per request: either set thinking_token_budget in each target workspace model's Advanced Params and let the router pick the model, or write body['thinking_token_budget'] in the filter.
kept.expected_gain: Simple questions skip up to 512 thinking tokens. At 46-61 tok/s that is up to about 8-11 s saved, so a trivial question drops from 3-8 s to about 1-2 s. Sticky Pro avoids repeated cross-engine re-prefill: moving a 10-15k-token chat from Gemma to the dense 27B Qwen means a cold prefill on :8001, plausibly several seconds (measure it). Ping-ponging would pay that cost every switch. Quality on hard prompts should not drop, because they still get thinking or Pro. The 'When to Reason' semantic-router paper reports 47.1% lower latency and 48.5% fewer tokens with +10.2 pp on MMLU-Pro when reasoning is applied selectively.
evidence: https://ai.google.dev/gemma/docs/capabilities/thinking (Gemma 4: <|think|> token inserted in a system turn at the start of the prompt; 26B with thinking off adds an empty thought channel; strip earlier thoughts from history)

https://docs.vllm.ai/features/reasoning_outputs.html (Gemma 4 reasoning toggled via chat_template_kwargs enable_thinking; request-level overrides --default-chat-template-kwargs; thinking budget control section)
https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.08731v1 / https://research.ibm.com/publications/when-to-reason-semantic-router-for-vllm (selective reasoning: -47.1% latency, -48.5% tokens, +10.2 pp MMLU-Pro)
https://vllm.ai/blog/2025-09-11-semantic-router (fast path vs chain-of-thought path routing design)
kept.applies_to_our_stack: You already use thinking_token_budget and --enable-prefix-caching on both engines, and Gemma's TTFT of 0.15-0.25 s depends on cache hits, so protecting the prefix is the main latency lever. vLLM's docs do not list Gemma 4 under thinking-budget control. You say it works for you, but verify that budget=0 actually stops thinking cleanly with the gemma4 reasoning parser (a stray '<|channel>' could leak). If it misbehaves, use 32-64 instead. Uzbek keyword lists need tuning to your real chats.
kept.risk: Low to medium. Heuristics can misroute: a tricky short question sent to the fast tier gives the trick-question failure you have already seen. Mitigate by putting '?' together with digits or comparatives in the think tier, and keep think, not fast, as the default when unsure.
kept.test_plan: Build a 20-prompt Uzbek set: 8 trivial, 6 web or factual, 6 hard or trick. Run it through 'Sarob' (always 512) and 'Sarob Auto' using the /api/chat/completions API with stream timing, recording time-to-first-content-token and total time. In the :8000 logs, check that 'Prefix cache hit rate' stays high across a 5-turn chat where tiers alternate fast/think. If it drops sharply, something in the prompt prefix is changing. kept.title: Keep the prompt prefix byte-stable: move the per-turn <memory_context> block out of the system message and remove minute-level date/time variables
kept.what_to_change:
PROBLEM, confirmed in the Open WebUI v0.12.0 source: utils/memory.py add_memory_context() runs a vector query over the last 7 user messages (k=8) and appends '<memory_context>...[User Memory]...[Relevant Context]...</memory_context>' to the END OF THE SYSTEM MESSAGE (add_or_update_system_message(..., append=True)). The 'Relevant Context' part changes almost every turn, so the token stream differs right after the ~1.8k system prompt. vLLM prefix caching can then reuse only the static head, and the whole chat history (plus every old image, through the vision encoder) is prefilled again on each new user turn. Hops inside one turn still hit the cache because memory does not change within a turn.
FIX: add an Open WebUI Filter Function that uses the request() hook (added in v0.11.2, runs before EVERY model call and after memory injection). Enable it globally or on Sarob, Sarob Tez and Pro, with Valves priority=999 so it runs after other filters. Paste-ready code that also covers recommendation 2:

"""
title: Sarob Context Slimmer
version: 0.1.0
"""
import re
from typing import Optional
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
MEM_RE = re.compile(r"\s*<memory_context>.*?</memory_context>\s*", re.S)
TOOL_IMG_TXT = "Here are the images from the tool results above"
IMG = {"image_url", "input_image", "image"}
def _t(c):
    if isinstance(c, str): return c
    return "".join(p.get("text", "") for p in (c or []) if isinstance(p, dict) and p.get("type") in ("text", "input_text"))
class Filter:
    class Valves(BaseModel):
        priority: int = Field(default=999)
        move_memory: bool = True
        keep_image_turns: int = Field(default=1)
        old_tool_chars: int = Field(default=1500)
    def __init__(self): self.valves = self.Valves()
    async def request(self, body: dict, __user__: Optional[dict] = None) -> dict:
        msgs = body.get("messages") or []
        users = [i for i, m in enumerate(msgs) if m.get("role") == "user" and TOOL_IMG_TXT not in _t(m.get("content"))]
        if not users: return body
        last_u = users[-1]
        k = max(1, self.valves.keep_image_turns)
        cut = users[-k] if len(users) >= k else 0
        s = msgs[0] if msgs and msgs[0].get("role") == "system" else None
        if self.valves.move_memory and s and isinstance(s.get("content"), str):
            mm = MEM_RE.search(s["content"])
            if mm:
                mem = mm.group(0).strip()
                s["content"] = MEM_RE.sub("\n", s["content"]).strip()
                u = msgs[last_u]
                if "<memory_context>" not in _t(u.get("content")):
                    u["content"] = (mem + "\n\n" + u["content"]) if isinstance(u["content"], str) else [{"type": "text", "text": mem}, *u["content"]]
        for i in range(last_u):
            m, c = msgs[i], msgs[i].get("content")
            if m.get("role") == "tool" and isinstance(c, str) and len(c) > self.valves.old_tool_chars:
                m["content"] = c[:self.valves.old_tool_chars] + f"\n[eski vosita natijasi qisqartirildi: {len(c)} belgi]"
            if i < cut and isinstance(c, list):
                n = sum(1 for p in c if isinstance(p, dict) and p.get("type") in IMG)
                if n:
                    m["content"] = [p for p in c if not (isinstance(p, dict) and p.get("type") in IMG)] + [{"type": "text", "text": f"[{n} ta eski rasm kontekstdan olib tashlandi]"}]
        return body

Open WebUI 0.12 includes native compaction (utils/context_compaction.py), off by default. When the estimated tokens exceed the threshold, it summarizes the oldest turns with a task model, persists the summary on the checkpoint message ('contextSummary'), and sends '[CONVERSATION SUMMARY]\n...' appended to the system message plus only the recent turns. Settings (env, or Admin UI; env applies only on first boot unless ENABLE_PERSISTENT_CONFIG=False):
ENABLE_CONTEXT_COMPACTION=true
CONTEXT_COMPACTION_TOKEN_THRESHOLD=28000 (default 80000 is too high for latency on Spark)
CONTEXT_COMPACTION_TOKEN_CAP=28000
CONTEXT_COMPACTION_RETENTION_PERCENTAGE=40 (clamped 10-50; share of messages kept verbatim)
CONTEXT_COMPACTION_MODEL=<model id of your Gemma no-think task model> (falls back to the chat model if unset)
CONTEXT_COMPACTION_PROMPT_TEMPLATE=<Uzbek version of the default; must keep {{PREVIOUS_SUMMARY}}, {{COMPACTED_MESSAGES}}, {{RECENT_MESSAGES}}; tell it to keep exact numbers, URLs, file names and user preferences, and to answer in Uzbek, at most 300 words>.
Per-model override: in each model's Advanced Params add custom param compact_token_threshold (read from metadata.params), for example 20000 for Pro (Qwen3.8 dense, slower prefill) and 28000 for Sarob.
Note: the estimator counts len(text)//4 per token and 1,000 tokens per image. Uzbek Latin on Gemma/Qwen tokenizers is probably about 3-3.5 chars per token, so the real count is about 15-30% higher than the estimate; 28000 estimated is roughly 32-36k real tokens.

Cost: one blocking summary call when the threshold is crossed (prefill about 25k at about 3-4k tok/s plus about 400-800 output tokens at about 55 tok/s, so roughly 10-20 s once). Confirm that the 'Compacting context' status appears, that the Open WebUI log contains 'Compacted chat context ... dropped=N kept=M', and ask 3 recall questions about compacted turns. Time the turn that triggers compaction. Also force compaction during a web-search turn to check the second-system-message case does not raise a template error in the vLLM logs. Then set the production value of 28000. About 15 minutes.
kept.verifier_reason: The env names check out in config.py: ENABLE_CONTEXT_COMPACTION (default False), CONTEXT_COMPACTION_TOKEN_THRESHOLD (80000), CONTEXT_COMPACTION_TOKEN_CAP (defaults to the threshold if unset), CONTEXT_COMPACTION_RETENTION_PERCENTAGE (40, clamped 10-50), CONTEXT_COMPACTION_PROMPT_TEMPLATE and CONTEXT_COMPACTION_MODEL. In the visible config.py these are plain os.getenv reads, not PersistentConfig, so the claim that env applies only on first boot unless ENABLE_PERSISTENT_CONFIG=False is not supported. Each compaction rewrites the system message and breaks the prefix once, which is acceptable. The mid-loop second-system-message risk for the Gemma 4 and Qwen templates is real and must be tested.
